essence: What is rewarded right away gets repeated.
modern_lens: Chapter 15 explains that the brain values immediate rewards over delayed ones. Most good habits pay off later, while bad habits pay off now. The fix is to add a small, immediate reward to good habits and to make the cost of bad habits felt sooner. It works for team rituals as well as personal routines.

ideas.name: Repeated When Rewarded
ideas.text: Behaviours followed by an immediate, satisfying feeling get repeated; behaviours followed by an unpleasant one get avoided. Pleasure tells the brain that a behaviour is worth remembering and doing again.
ideas.try: Notice how you feel in the minute after your habit. Is anything satisfying happening?

ideas.name: Living in a Delayed-Return World
ideas.text: Human brains evolved for immediate returns: eat now, rest now. Modern life mostly pays later: save now, retire later; study now, earn later. That mismatch is why good long-term habits often feel unrewarding in the moment.
ideas.try: List one good habit whose payoff is months away and one small payoff it could give today.

ideas.name: Present Bias
ideas.text: We value the present more than the future. Bad habits usually feel good now and cost later; good habits usually cost now and pay later. To keep a good habit, give it some of the immediate feeling it lacks.
ideas.try: For one bad habit, write the immediate benefit and the delayed cost side by side.

ideas.name: Add an Instant Reward
ideas.text: Finish a good habit with a small immediate reward that fits who you want to be: a satisfying tick on a chart, a favourite tea after a workout, moving money into a trip fund each time you skip a takeaway.
ideas.try: Pick one small reward to enjoy straight after your habit, and use it every time for two weeks.

ideas.name: Make Avoidance Visible
ideas.text: Habits of avoidance, such as not buying, not drinking or not snacking, give you nothing to see. Make them visible: transfer the money you did not spend into a named account, or mark each day you did without.
ideas.try: Open a named savings pot and move money into it each time you resist a bad habit.
